title: Spectral Séance: Lamp-Driven Skull Revelation
description: A glowing iridescent lamp sits on a dark pedestal. A ghostly skull floats nearby, barely visible through heavy fog. The user adjusts post-processing bloom, volumetric god-rays, and a custom color-grading pass to reveal the skull's hidden spectral aura, then toggles a film-grain noise pass and tweaks its intensity to finalize a haunted photograph captured via a screenshot button.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with EffectComposer from three/addons. Load IridescenceLamp.glb and place it at (-1.5, 0, 0) on a dark circular pedestal. Load ScatteringSkull.glb and place it floating at (1.5, 1, 0) with a slow sinusoidal hover animation. Set the scene background to near-black (#0a0a0f). Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 5) looking at origin with OrbitControls. Add a dim ambient light (intensity 0.15) and a PointLight inside the lamp model (intensity 3, color #88ffee) that casts shadows. Build an EffectComposer pipeline with these passes in order: (1) RenderPass, (2) UnrealBloomPass with threshold 0.2, strength 1.5, radius 0.8, (3) a ShaderPass implementing screen-space god-rays emanating from the lamp's screen-space position toward the skull using a radial blur sampling approach (10 samples), (4) a ShaderPass for color grading with uniforms for hue-shift, saturation, and brightness, (5) a ShaderPass for film-grain noise with a time-based random pattern and an intensity uniform, (6) OutputPass. Create a dat.gui or lil-gui panel with these interactions: Step 1 — a slider for bloom strength (0 to 3). Step 2 — a slider for god-ray intensity (0 to 1). Step 3 — a hue-shift slider (-PI to PI) that tints the entire scene, revealing hidden spectral colors on the skull when shifted to purple range. Step 4 — a saturation slider (0 to 2). Step 5 — a film-grain intensity slider (0 to 0.5). Step 6 — a 'Capture Séance' button that calls renderer.domElement.toDataURL and opens the image in a new tab. The skull should have an emissive material override (emissive #220033, emissiveIntensity 0.4) applied after loading so it glows faintly. Ensure the god-ray shader recalculates the lamp light screen position each frame by projecting the PointLight world position. All shaders must compile without errors. The final visual should feel like a haunted supernatural photograph.
